rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis proposes adding W to TiVNbTa to form TiVNbTaW, whereas the hidden target compares CrFeTaVW with CrFeTiVW (Ta substituted by Ti) using simulations and mechanical alloying/SPS. These are different kinds of interventions—compositional modification of a different base alloy system versus a Ta/Ti substitution in a CrFeVW system—so the intervention type differs.
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis specifies quasi-static mechanical testing from room temperature to 1273 K. The hidden target uses MD/MC simulations from 300–2100 K and SPS consolidation at 1543–1573 K, with thermal diffusivity measured from 300–1000 K. The regimes are different: mechanical testing versus thermal diffusivity measurement and simulation of segregation.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis invokes W-induced solid-solution strengthening and a shift from screw to edge dislocation slip to retain high-temperature strength. The hidden target's mechanism involves MC-driven segregation, Laves-phase formation from Fe–Ta mixing enthalpy, and phonon mean free path effects on thermal diffusivity. These are different classes of mechanism—mechanical strengthening versus phase stability and thermal transport.
rationale.outcome_agreement: The hypothesis predicts improved high-temperature yield strength retention. The hidden target predicts similar thermal diffusivity for both alloys and altered phase constitution (bcc + Laves vs. two bcc phases), with no mechanical strength measurements. The predicted properties and directions are unrelated.
